I hit the tool limit mid-slice, so let me hand you what's solid rather than a half-built archive.

First: your build is red
dotnet build is failing on two errors, both the same line:

tests/MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tests/Displays/DisplayDevicePairingTests.cs line 144

csharp
Assert.DoesNotContain(':', result.DeviceSecret, StringComparison.Ordinal);
A char first argument makes the compiler pick DoesNotContain<char>(char, IAsyncEnumerable<char>, IEqualityComparer<char>) — hence "cannot convert from string to IAsyncEnumerable<char>". xUnit's three-argument StringComparison overload only exists for a string needle. One-character fix:

csharp
Assert.DoesNotContain(":", result.DeviceSecret, StringComparison.Ordinal);
Everything else in the terminal log is green: 459 tests, 0 failed, --smoke passes, no outdated packages.

Where the tree actually is
M2 and M3 are both closed out (Slice 4 — display devices — landed, plus the /account profile close-out and the CSS fixes). BUILD_PROGRESS.md ends with "Next: M4 — ordering." So the next step is M4 Slice 1, and I'd scope it to DataAccess only — no Razor — because the compiler-catch risk lives in components and I'd rather land the engine green first.

What I have written and reviewed
These are complete and I verified the API details against real sources rather than from memory:

src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Menu/MenuDirectory.cs — read side only; returns inactive items too, per §7's "the guest sees that the salmon exists and is out"
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Orders/OrderEventVocabulary.cs — the enum↔SQL-string mapping, both directions in one file
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Orders/OrderEventLog.cs — two queries (headers, then the five operation tables folded by UNION ALL with every branch cast to its target type), shared by the log reader and the transaction
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Orders/OrderReadModel.cs — over the §8.3 views; note order_current_state's counts are bigint and needed a ::int cast
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Orders/OrderMutations.cs — §6.6 verbatim: FOR SHARE sitting → INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + FOR UPDATE order → max(sequence)+1 → validate → insert event/operations/kitchen_notification → commit
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Orders/OrderWorkflow.cs and OrdersServiceCollectionExtensions.cs
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Program.cs — full file, with AddRestaurantOrders() added after displays
DisplayDevicePairingTests.cs — full file with the fix above
Two things I checked rather than assumed: Dapper's FeatureSupport.Get still returns the Postgres profile for NpgsqlConnection, so = ANY(@Identifiers) binds a Guid[] as one uuid[] parameter instead of being expanded into (@p1,@p2); and every row type uses DateTime/long/int to match what Npgsql actually returns, projected to DateTimeOffset afterward — the constructor-binding trap that bit TableDirectory and PersonDirectory.

Two behaviours worth vetoing now if you disagree: the server prices every line-add from menu_item.price_amount, staff edits included (§6.5.4 only says it for guest submissions, but the counter has price_adjustment with a mandatory reason for deviations); and AppendToLivingOrderAsync refuses to lazily create an order in a closed sitting, returning OrderNotFound — §6.7 corrections append to history, they shouldn't invent it.

The test files. Shipping the source without the tests would break slice discipline, so I haven't packed a tar.gz. Say continue and I'll finish the tests and hand you the complete archive in one go.

M4 Slice 1 — the order engine. Extracts at the repo root, 14 files, 13 new and one edit.

bash
tar -xzf m4-slice1-order-engine.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
cat docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.append.md >> docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md && rm docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.append.md
Files to delete: none.

Two things to check before you extract. I deliberately left DisplayDevicePairingTests.cs out — you already fixed it, and overwriting your fix buys nothing. Program.cs is in there, rebuilt from the dump plus two additions; if you've edited it since, extract everything else and apply those two lines by hand (they're quoted verbatim at the end of _CHANGES.md).

No Razor this slice, on purpose. All three M4 surfaces are renderings of one transaction and two projections, and building a staging area on an untested write path means debugging components and row-level locking at once.

What's in it. DapperOrderMutations is §6.6 verbatim — FOR SHARE the sitting, FOR UPDATE the order (created lazily via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + re-select, which is §6.1's "lost creation race is re-read and proceeds"), max(sequence)+1 under that lock, validate, then event + operations + kitchen_notification in one transaction or none of them. DapperOrderReadModel covers the four §8.3 views; DapperOrderEventLog reads the raw log in two queries. OrderWorkflow is the post-commit shell that surfaces call instead — it publishes the §9 notifications and records the §12 counters, and it publishes KitchenAlert only when the transaction actually wrote the row rather than re-deriving §10.1, so the sound and the stored record can't drift.

Three things worth your veto. The server prices every line-add including staff edits — §6.5.4 only says it for guest submissions, but the counter has price_adjustment for deviations, which demands a reason. A post-close administrative correction still chimes the kitchen, because §10.1 has no closed-sitting exception and I implemented it literally. And a rejected first send returns an order identifier for a row that no longer exists — useful when the order already existed, a trap if a caller persists it.

One finding. The §8.5 equivalence test compares the line set, not row order. Lines in one send share an occurred_at to the microsecond, and the tie-breakers can't agree: the fold's ThenBy(Guid) uses .NET's Guid.CompareTo (Data1 as an int, then two shorts, then bytes) while the view uses PostgreSQL's bytewise uuid collation. Neither is wrong, and §8.5's own wording never claimed an ordering. Same reasoning cuts through intra-event operation order, so I corrected OrderEventLog's doc comment — its read order is deterministic but is not an insertion order.

Expect OrderReadModelTests to be your slowest test: it drives 60 seeded-random events through the real transaction before comparing.

Manual verification needs a menu and there's no surface for one until M5 — two INSERTs are in the checklist. Next slice is the staging area and the living-order view on /table/{id}.
